title: What is AWS Lambda? - AWS Lambda

chunks.content: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service. With Lambda, you can run code without provisioning or managing servers. Lambda automatically manages the underlying infrastructure – including server maintenance, capacity provisioning, scaling, and patching – so you can focus on your application logic. Lambda provides three compute primitives, each designed for different workload patterns: Lambda Event Functions – Run code in response to events or API calls without managing servers. You write a handler function, connect it to a trigger (API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, EventBridge, and 200+ other AWS services), and Lambda executes it. Each invocation runs independently with no shared state, scaling horizontally to match demand. Lambda manages execution environments, scaling, routing, and fault tolerance. Lambda Event Functions – Run code in response to events or API calls without managing servers. You write a handler function, connect it to a trigger (API Gateway, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, EventBridge, and 200+ other AWS services), and Lambda executes it. Each invocation runs independently with no shared state, scaling horizontally to match demand. Lambda manages execution environments, scaling, routing, and fault tolerance. Lambda Web Functions – Run web applications and API backends as HTTP servers. Your Node.js code listens on a port and handles HTTP requests directly, using web frameworks such as Express, Hono, or React Router without adapters. Each execution environment serves multiple concurrent requests. Lambda provides an HTTPS endpoint, scales your application based on traffic (including to zero), and can replicate it across AWS Regions. Lambda Web Functions – Run web applications and API backends as HTTP servers. Your Node.js code listens on a port and handles HTTP requests directly, using web frameworks such as Express, Hono, or React Router without adapters. Each execution environment serves multiple concurrent requests. Lambda provides an HTTPS endpoint, scales your application based on traffic (including to zero), and can replicate it across AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs – Isolated compute environments with near-instant startup and a total lifespan of up to 8 hours (including both running and suspended time). Designed for workloads needing a dedicated compute environment for each individual user or job. Lambda manages isolation, capacity, and networking. Your application uses Lambda MicroVMs APIs and HTTPS endpoints to connect each user/job to their compute environment. chunks.content: Event Functions is the name for the original Lambda function type that runs your code in response to events and API calls. The name distinguishes this function type from Lambda Web Functions and Lambda MicroVMs , and the Lambda console labels it Event function . The underlying resource is unchanged: the API operations (such as CreateFunction and Invoke ), the AWS SDKs, the AWS CLI, the AWS::Lambda::Function resource type, and ARNs continue to use function , so you don't need to change any code, infrastructure templates, or IAM permissions. For pricing information, see AWS Lambda Pricing .

chunks.content: Lambda Event Functions, Lambda Web Functions, and Lambda MicroVMs share a common serverless foundation: No server management – AWS manages underlying infrastructure, instance patching, and capacity. No server management – AWS manages underlying infrastructure, instance patching, and capacity. Pay-per-use billing – No upfront commitments. You pay only for the resources used. Pay-per-use billing – No upfront commitments. You pay only for the resources used. Managed networking – All three provide service-managed inbound and outbound network access. Managed networking – All three provide service-managed inbound and outbound network access. Firecracker virtualization – VM-level isolation between workloads. Firecracker virtualization – VM-level isolation between workloads. While they share this foundation, they serve different use cases: Lambda Event Functions Lambda Web Functions Lambda MicroVMs Best for Request-response or event-driven workloads (APIs, data processing, automation) Web applications and API backends that serve HTTP traffic directly Persistent environments running user or AI-produced untrusted code Programming model Function handler invoked in a supported runtime HTTP server that listens on a port, using standard web frameworks Any application – run your own binaries, listen on ports, use Linux OS capabilities Duration Up to 15 minutes per invocation by default; up to 90 minutes per asynchronous or event source mapping invocation on Lambda Managed Instances; multi-step workflows lasting up to a year with Lambda Durable Functions Up to 15 minutes per HTTP request (default 30 seconds) Up to 8 hours per session; suspend and resume across sessions Runtime environment Service-provided language runtimes; support for customer-provided runtimes Service-provided Node.js runtimes Customer-provided MicroVM images Inbound Networking Direct invocations or event-source integrations with AWS services Service-provided HTTPS endpoint with TLS; optional latency-based routing across AWS Regions Inbound access to any port using OSI Layer 7 protocols Concurrency One request per execution environment at a time by default; multiple concurrent requests per execution environment for Lambda Managed Instances Multiple concurrent requests per execution environment Multiple concurrent connections per MicroVM Environment State Execution environments can be reused (warm starts), but state might not persist across invocations Execution environments can be reused (warm starts), but state might not persist across invocations Memory and disk state preserved on suspend; restored on resume Scaling Automatic – Lambda creates and destroys execution environments in response to traffic Automatic – Lambda creates and destroys execution environments in response to traffic, scaling to zero when idle Developer-controlled – you create, suspend, resume, and terminate MicroVMs through the API Lifecycle Fully managed by Lambda Fully managed by Lambda Developer-controlled; optional idle policies for automatic suspend-resume Pricing Per-request + GB-seconds of execution time Per request, plus active CPU time (billed in 1 ms increments) and memory for each execution environment's lifetime Per-second of compute while running + snapshot storage while suspended Thanks for letting us know we're doing a good job!
